_comment: R2.4. Base-tier crafting: orb_basic and potion_small from gathered materials, at the campfire. CLAUDE.md: data that varies per recipe lives here, never in gameplay code.
_comment_scope: GAME_DESIGN.md 15 / MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md 10: baseline materials are wood, stone, fiber and berries and nothing else -- SD18 built the Rootstone tier above these in `data/recipes/recipes_rootstone.json` rather than growing this one; `item_db.gd` merges both files into one recipe book.
_comment_cost: `cost` is a list of {id, n} against autoload/inventory.gd, the same shape data/items/buildables.json already uses for build costs -- one format for 'what does this take'.
_comment_output: `output` is {id, n}: what one craft produces. Always one craft at a time; there is no bulk-craft multiplier here.
_comment_unlock: OF30. `unlocked_by` is an OPTIONAL autoload/progression_state.gd flag id. A recipe with no `unlocked_by` is known from the first minute (potion_small); a recipe that names one is not listed in the craft screen and cannot be crafted until that flag is set. Read through item_db.recipe_unlock_flag() and answered by game_state.recipe_known(). Deliberately a plain flag rather than a recipe-book system: the flag store already exists, already saves, and already loads, and a second parallel 'what do I know' list is the kind of speculative machinery CLAUDE.md's working-style section says not to build.
_comment_unlock_orb: Mira hands over the orb recipe during the required first village visit, alongside the early gathering tools; that line writes `recipe_orb_basic` and the craft screen gains a row. Grandpa's opening gift of fifteen Orbs is untouched: the player has Orbs from minute one, and what Mira adds is never running out of them again. TUNABLE, and cheap on purpose (spec: basic Orbs are affordable) -- three wood and two fiber is one deadwood node and half a grass node.

_comment_r7_6: R7.6. `hoe` and `berry_seeds` join the tool block above under exactly its rule: ungated, because the material cost is the gate and a flag on top would gate the same door twice. The hoe is priced between the knife and the axe -- it is the cheapest way into farming and is meant to be, since it buys the player nothing until they also have seeds and a bed. `berry_seeds` turns 3 berries into 4, which is the one number that decides whether farming is a loop or a leak: at 4-for-3 a single wild picking (3 berries, data/config/harvest.json) seeds four beds that return 4 each, so the farm pays for itself on the first crop and the player is never stranded with plots and no seed. It is also why the seed recipe is not gated behind the hoe -- somebody who sells their hoe should still be able to sow the beds they already tilled. Mira sells seeds too (data/config/trade.json), for a player who would rather spend coin than berries. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_tools: Owner brief section 4/5: 'use the workbench to craft capture orbs, knives, axes, pickaxes and other equipment.' Tam's gifts stay the tutorial path (village_tam_tools -- free, guaranteed, first conversation); these recipes are what makes a REPLACEMENT possible when a tool breaks or a second one is wanted, so losing an axe is an errand rather than a dead end. Ungated on purpose: the material cost is the gate (a tool costs real stone, which needs the pickaxe loop or bare-handed scraping), and a flag on top would gate the same door twice -- recipes_rootstone.json's own _comment_unlock argues exactly this for orb_greater. All costs TUNABLE.
